ATHLETICS

Boss level: showing up for other people, then showing up for myself.

CHAPTER 1: RUNNING THE FACILITY

Before I was running races, I was running a building. As an international student figuring out life in the US, I took on the role of Operations Supervisor for a 37,000 sq. ft. recreation facility at the University of Florida.

That meant leading and training a team of 7 associates and making sure the doors opened right, whether that was the 5 a.m. shift or the 11 p.m. closing crew. We served 50,000+ students and somehow still managed to pick up more than 50 five star Google reviews along the way.

Behind the scenes, I also managed end to end inventory using Fusion and Connect 2 ERP systems, keeping PO records straight for high value athletic equipment so gear was ready and available for every major competitive event on campus.

Wrapping up a year with UF RecSports

Even outside the facility, I stayed close to the recreation and wellness community, showing up at conferences and roundtables to talk about how student rec centers can do right by the people who use them every day.

Working in operations taught me that fitness is not just something I chase for myself. It is something I help build for other people too.

Florida RecWell business meeting

CHAPTER 2: THE RUNNING JOURNEY BEGINS

I spent eight years in the gym before I ever laced up for a real run. Once I started running though, it did not stay a small hobby for long. My first half marathon turned into several more, and eventually that mileage built up into a full marathon.

Along the way I also got hooked on obstacle racing, taking on a Spartan 5K and a Spartan 10K, crawling through mud and under wire because normal race day was starting to feel too easy.

Half Marathons Full Marathon Spartan 5K Spartan 10K

Bib 94, 39th Pune International Marathon

Obstacle racing has a way of humbling you fast. Barbed wire, mud pits, and a headband that says Spartan are not exactly a comfortable place to be, but they are a great place to find out what you are actually made of.

Every crawl, climb, and carry became part of the same story that started in the weight room and turned into something much bigger.

Down in the mud at a Spartan race

CHAPTER 3: TEAM ENERGY

None of this happened alone. Training and racing became a lot more fun once it turned into something shared with a team.

Track squad, gym family, and HYROX teammates who made the grind fun

HYROX became the next test, a mix of running and functional strength work that does not let you hide from either one. Rope pulls, sled pushes, and a finish line that never seems to arrive fast enough.

Crossing that finish line, soaked and grinning under the lights, is the kind of feeling that keeps you signing up for the next one.

Finish line at a HYROX event

CHAPTER 4: TURNING IT INTO A CRAFT

While working through my master's degree, I made time to get my knowledge and passion for fitness validated the right way. I earned a personal training certification from the National Association of Sports Medicine (NASM), an internationally recognized and NCAA accredited credential.

Once certified, I started coaching people directly, helping them build strength, get into the best shape of their life, and feel more confident in their own bodies. It turned years of personal trial and error into something I could hand off to someone else and watch actually work for them.

NASM Certified Personal Trainer NCAA Accredited
